column1: # Batch 33 — supplychain: what was probed and did NOT ship, kept as data.
# Two kinds of row are here. The first is a candidate that PASSED the probe
# and was dropped anyway, because the probe counts records and cannot see
# whether they are the right records — read those first, they are the ones
# that cost something to find. The second is a candidate the engine or this
# environment's network policy ruled out before it could be measured.
# Hosts in the third block answered nothing at all: the egress policy in the
# environment this batch was authored in permits package-registry hosts and
# refuses everything else at CONNECT (HTTP 403 from the gateway). They are
# recorded so a session with wider egress knows what has already been looked
# at rather than re-deriving the list.

column3: what happened

https://rubygems.org/api/v1/gems/{q}.json — probe PASS, 2107 bytes. The gem record is the ROOT OBJECT and the document's only array is dependencies.runtime (13 entries for rails), so the engine emitted 13 dependency records and the gem's own fields — authors, licenses, sha, the whole project/source/changelog/funding URI block — reached nothing. Declaring array_path=dependencies.runtime would have made it a forward-dependency row, but then dependencies.development is dropped, and the endpoint cannot be declared twice (one GET, one declared array). Dropped: RUBYGEMS_OWNER_GEMS emits the full gem record per gem and rubygems.org/api/v1/versions/{q}.json was already registered.

https://pub.dev/api/packages/{q}/metrics — probe PASS (json:score.tags, 22 items). Run through the engine it mined "scorecard.panaReport.report.sections" (5 records) out of 6 candidate arrays, runner-up "scorecard.weeklyVersionDownloads.minorRangeWeeklyDownloads" (5), and stored five analysis-report SECTION headings titled "Follow Dart file conventions", "Provide documentation", "Platform support". The document has no array that is its record set — the metrics ARE the root object — and there is no way to declare that while a denser array exists. Dropped.

HTTP 200 with {"objects":[],"total":0} for real scopes (tried babel). An EMPTY_RESULTSET by construction — the qualifier is not supported by the search index — which is the failure mode CLAUDE.md rule 1 names explicitly: a source verified live that emits nothing on every run, forever.

HTTP 200, 1462 bytes, but "versions" is an array of STRINGS ("3.5.8", "4.0.1", …), not of records. NUGET_REGISTRATION_INDEX covers the same ground as 86 real version records with the registry's own commit trail attached.

HTTP 200, 12.2 MB — "packageNames" is an array of 470,134 bare STRINGS. The same namespace question is answered for PHP by PACKAGIST_POPULAR (ranked, with records) and the string list has no fields to key or query.

The crates.io sparse index is newline-delimited JSON: one complete JSON object per line, one line per version. hpengine has no NDJSON mode and HP_JSON parses only the first object, so declaring it would discard every version but the oldest. The same data is CRATESIO_CRATE_VERSIONS, which is a real JSON array.
Same NDJSON shape — one {Path, Version, Timestamp} object per line. This is the global Go module publish firehose and is worth having; it needs an NDJSON mode in the engine, not a row.

HTTP 200 and live, but a single 189 MB document with no paging and no incremental form. api.anaconda.org, which the tree already registers and which serves the same data per package, is not reachable under this environment's policy.
A fixed FIRST page of the NuGet catalog. Declaring it is a first-only read by construction (house rule 2); the catalog index itself is already registered.

HTTP 401 — the npm user document requires authentication. NPM_MAINTAINER_PACKAGES answers the same question (which packages does this account publish) through the public search index.
